sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is among the smallest species of the genus, head length (to the anterior margin of the clypeus) 2.37—3.11 mm; in some samples, however, it can be as large as the smallest soldiers of I. severus. The mandible is most evenly curved from base to apex (tied with I. planifrons, difference of the log curvature of the left mandible 0.85—1.88). The worker and its enteric valve are the smallest in the genus, the enteric valve usually of the muneris type; in about 2% of samples the enteric valve is intermediate between the fungifaber and finitimus types. The alate is on average, together with I. phalloides, the smallest in the genus, head width (across the compound eyes) 1.40—1.61 mm. Ecology and distribution: always found in evergreen forest, from Côte d'Ivoire to Gabon, less than 300 km from the Atlantic coast, building mushroom-shaped epigeal nests (to which the specific name refers).

note: Adapted from the species-level diagnosis in the revision by Josens et al. (2025), original in English; the measurement abbreviations have been replaced by descriptive Chinese names in line with the definitions of the original table. This entry records the diagnostic characters and ecological points of that revision and does not transcribe its morphological description paragraphs or measurement tables.
